finding: On the macOS runner the Windows visual capability probe reproduced all 17 recorded Windows outcomes, but VisualTestCapabilityProbeTest rejected the five qmp-peer-af-unix-absent cases: their final line carried the interpreter's name suggestion after the recorded AttributeError.
cause: The probe removes socket.AF_UNIX in the QMP peer child (prefix 'import socket as _windows;del _windows.AF_UNIX;'), whose 'server=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX)' then raises AttributeError; VisualTargetTests.server fails with the child's stderr, so the case's final line is the child's traceback line. CPython 3.15 traceback suggestions check the first 20 public attributes of the module for a nested match when no close name exists; socket.AF_APPLETALK is a socket.AddressFamily member and AddressFamily still defines AF_UNIX, so it appends ". Did you mean '.AF_APPLETALK.AF_UNIX' instead of '.AF_UNIX'?". Windows CPython has no AF_UNIX in socket or AddressFamily and CPython 3.10 to 3.14 have no nested suggestion, so their line ends at the message. The comparison normalized only the [WinError n]/[Errno n] prefix.
